courses.name: Topics: Intro to Networking & Security
courses.desc: Advanced topics course covering network infrastructure design, protocol security, encryption standards, and defense-in-depth strategies for enterprise environments. Capstone deliverable: a full structured cabling design for a multi-floor university building.
highlights: Designed a Cat 5e extended-star topology for Constant Hall at ODU — covering all floors, MER/TC placement, and cable-run estimation
Produced a complete materials budget and sourcing plan; applied TIA/EIA-568 structured cabling standards
Delivered the design as a stakeholder-ready PDF presentation
Explored PKI frameworks, certificate authorities, and FIDO authentication standards
Studied IPv6 security implications and transition vulnerabilities
Analyzed SSO implementations and authentication protocols across enterprise environments

courses.name: Introduction to Cybersecurity
courses.desc: A hands-on introduction to defensive cybersecurity built around 15 lab exercises spanning firewalls, intrusion detection, packet and log analysis, incident response, and enterprise identity — plus written research on breach case studies and security-policy design.
highlights: Completed 15 hands-on labs: pfSense firewall hardening, NAT & remote access, wireless security, Windows/Linux security policies, and closing security holes
Ran intrusion detection with Snort and performed packet analysis with Wireshark and NetworkMiner
Log analysis and incident-response & forensics labs — the direct foundation for my Mini SIEM Dashboard project
Configured Active Directory in an enterprise environment and applied patching, anti-virus, and endpoint hardening
Wrote a short research paper designing a corporate security policy — a governance/GRC artifact identifying five priority issues
Authored a research paper analyzing the 2013 Target data breach

courses.name: Linux System for Cybersecurity
courses.desc: Hands-on Linux administration and system security covering user management, file permissions, shell scripting, and security hardening on Kali Linux. 11 labs completed across the semester.
highlights: Managed user/group accounts and configured access-control policies on Kali Linux
Deep-dive into SGID and sticky-bit permissions for shared-directory security
Bash scripting lab: automated a rotating backup system using crontab task scheduling
NAT vs. Bridged networking in VirtualBox / Kali — traffic isolation and attack-surface analysis
Password-cracking lab using John the Ripper on hashed credential files

courses.name: Cyber Law
courses.desc: Legal frameworks governing cyberspace, including constitutional protections, digital privacy, government surveillance, whistleblower cases, and critical-infrastructure defense law.
highlights: Volt Typhoon tabletop exercise: simulated a Chinese state-sponsored attack on the Port of Virginia — detection, inter-agency response, and legal authorities under live pressure
Analyzed the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) — the foundational U.S. computer-crime statute — and its application to modern cases
Analyzed Fourth Amendment implications in digital surveillance and government access to electronic records
Researched Julian Assange / WikiLeaks and the tension between transparency and national security
Studied legal precedents in data-privacy regulation and cross-border enforcement

courses.name: Cybercriminology: Foundations
courses.desc: Study of criminal behavior in digital spaces, cybercrime typologies, digital forensics foundations, and the factors driving cybercriminal activity.
highlights: Studied cybercrime typologies and the factors driving online victimization
Researched hacker subcultures and motivations across hacktivism, insider threats, and organized cybercrime
Studied digital-forensics fundamentals, evidence handling, and chain of custody
Examined the evolution of cybercrime legislation and cross-border enforcement challenges

courses.name: Basic Cybersecurity Programming & Networking
courses.desc: Programming concepts and networking fundamentals applied to cybersecurity, including scripting, TCP/IP, subnetting, and network troubleshooting.
highlights: Built Python scripts for file parsing, input validation, and basic automation
Practiced subnetting, CIDR, and IP addressing through hands-on lab exercises
Captured and analyzed live network traffic using Wireshark
Completed socket-programming exercises using a client/server model

courses.name: Cybersecurity and the Social Sciences
courses.desc: Interdisciplinary study connecting cybersecurity to social-science research methods, human behavior, and the social dimensions of digital security.
highlights: Applied social-science research methods to cybersecurity case studies and surveys
Studied human factors in phishing susceptibility and social-engineering attacks
Explored cyber-victimization research and patterns of online risk behavior
Built a literature review connecting psychology and cyber-offending

courses.name: Cybersecurity, Technology, and Society
courses.desc: Exploration of cybersecurity's role in society, examining how technology intersects with culture, policy, ethics, and global security challenges.
highlights: Wrote reflection essays connecting the CIA triad to real-world breach case studies
Examined the societal impact of surveillance, data collection, and privacy policy
Analyzed cybersecurity risk in healthcare, finance, and critical-infrastructure sectors
Evaluated the ethical responsibilities of security practitioners in public and private roles

courses.name: Interdisciplinary Theory & Concepts
courses.desc: Writing-intensive course presenting cybersecurity as an interdisciplinary field, strengthening research methodology and APA-formatted academic writing.
highlights: Completed an APA-formatted essay on cybersecurity as an interdisciplinary field
Developed technical-writing skills for security documentation
Strengthened the ability to communicate complex concepts to non-technical audiences

courses.name: Introduction to Ethics
courses.desc: Ethical reasoning and moral philosophy, providing a critical framework for evaluating dilemmas in cybersecurity, privacy, and technology.
highlights: Compared utilitarian, deontological, and virtue-ethics frameworks in applied contexts
Applied ethical reasoning to real-world tech dilemmas including privacy, AI, and surveillance
Wrote argumentative papers defending positions on contested moral issues
Discussed the ethical responsibilities carried by cybersecurity professionals

courses.name: Introduction to Criminology
courses.desc: Foundational study of crime, justice systems, and sociological theories explaining criminal behavior — essential context for understanding cybercrime.
highlights: Studied classical, strain, and social-learning theories of criminal behavior
Explored the structure and function of the U.S. criminal justice system
Analyzed the relationship between crime, law, and social policy
Connected traditional criminology to emerging patterns in cybercrime
